successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy entity is defined as a standalone camelCase interface (not extending BaseEntity) with all 11 canonical fields, and its leaveType field is typed as the LeaveType enum imported from shared/types — not a raw string.
An IPolicyRepository interface and a PolicyRepository class implementing it exist, exposing exactly six operations: findById, findByLeaveType, findAllActive, create, update, and deactivate.
create persists a new leave_policies row using a parameterized INSERT with RETURNING *, and returns the fully mapped LeavePolicy entity (including server-generated createdAt/updatedAt).

update builds a dynamic SET clause from only the supplied mutable fields, sets updated_at, excludes id/createdAt/updatedAt from the mutable set, and returns the updated LeavePolicy or null when no row matches.
deactivate sets is_active to false and returns a boolean — true when a row was affected, false when no row matched — matching the rowCount-based convention of the employee softDelete.
findByLeaveType and findAllActive return arrays (empty array when no rows), and findById returns a single LeavePolicy or null — each using parameterized queries against the leave_policies table.
The policy barrel (index.ts) re-exports LeavePolicy, IPolicyRepository, PolicyRepository, and the Create/Update input interfaces so downstream modules import only through the public entry point.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/policy/policy.repository.test.ts cover every repository method for success (asserting the returned entity and the exact SQL/params via toHaveBeenCalledWith), the empty/null/zero-rowCount case, and error propagation (rejects.toThrow), using makeRow/makePolicy helper factories.

constraints: All SQL must use parameterized queries — no string-interpolated user input. Query parameter arrays must be typed as unknown[] (never any[]) to satisfy the HARNESS.json no-any rule.

All database access goes through the repository pattern (GP-001); the PolicyRepository must use the existing pool from shared/db/connection.ts — no new connection objects, no inline SQL outside the repository.
The repository must NOT write audit records. GP-002 audit enforcement is deferred to the service/controller layer (later phases); this phase builds only model + repository.

The policy module may depend only on shared/types and shared/db — it is a foundation module with no domain-module dependencies, preserving the acyclic dependency direction in the reconciled architecture.

Modules must import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the barrel must export the full public surface and downstream consumers must not reach into policy.model.ts or policy.repository.ts directly.

DB rows use snake_case columns (leave_policies table); the repository must map snake_case rows to the camelCase LeavePolicy model via a row-mapping function, mirroring the Employee repository's mapRowToEmployee pattern.

Tests must use bare import paths (modules/policy/..., shared/db/connection, shared/types/index) per jest.config moduleDirectories, mock shared/db/connection as { pool: { query: jest.fn() } }, and cast pool.query as jest.Mock — matching the employee test conventions.
outOfScope: PolicyService, PolicyController, policyRoutes, and policy.validation.ts (Zod schemas) — these are planned in later phases (validation schemas, controllers, routes) per the reconciled architecture; this phase delivers only model + repository + barrel.
Audit record writing for policy create/update/deactivate operations — deferred to the service/controller layer per GP-002 enforcement placement.
RBAC enforcement and HTTP route definitions for policy endpoints — deferred to the routes + app registration phase.
Database migrations for the leave_policies table — this phase assumes the table schema exists as specified in the reconciled architecture; migration creation is not part of this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy has exactly two lifecycle states — ACTIVE and INACTIVE — represented by the isActive boolean. Deactivation transitions ACTIVE→INACTIVE; there is no hard delete in this phase. The entity is never soft-deleted (no deletedAt field); deactivation is the only deactivation mechanism.

A LeavePolicy's leaveType is constrained to the LeaveType enum values (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity) defined in shared/types — the repository must round-trip this enum value to/from the leave_type column without loss or coercion to a generic string.

createdAt and updatedAt are server-managed timestamps (set via NOW() in SQL), never supplied or mutated by the caller; update() must always set updated_at = NOW() and must never include id or createdAt in the mutable field set.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns LeavePolicy or null when no row matches. Database errors propagate as rejected promises (unhandled rejection is forbidden per GP-006).
Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array when no rows). Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns LeavePolicy[] filtered to is_active = true (empty array when none). Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Persists a row and returns the created LeavePolicy with server-generated timestamps. Constraint violations (e.g. duplicate) propagate as rejected promises.

Applies only supplied mutable fields via a dynamic SET clause; returns updated LeavePolicy or null when no row matches. When no mutable fields are supplied, returns the existing entity without issuing an UPDATE. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Sets is_active = false; returns boolean true when a row was affected, false when no row matched. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The PolicyRepository must mirror the EmployeeRepository structural pattern: a private snake_case Row interface, a mapRowToLeavePolicy(row) function converting snake→camel, a module-level camelToSnake helper for dynamic UPDATE column mapping, params typed as unknown[], and the rowCount-based boolean return for deactivate matching softDelete's (result.rowCount ?? 0) > 0 convention.
The LeavePolicy model must be a standalone camelCase interface (not extending BaseEntity), mirroring how Employee is defined as a standalone interface despite BaseEntity existing in shared/types.

The LeaveType enum (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity) must be imported from shared/types and used as the type of LeavePolicy.leaveType — the repository must not redefine or widen this enum.
The repository must import and use the existing `pool` export from shared/db/connection.ts — the same pg Pool instance used by the EmployeeRepository — rather than constructing a new Pool.

The policy repository test must follow the employee test's structure: jest.mock('shared/db/connection'), bare import paths, makeRow/makePolicy factories with spread overrides, per-method success + null/empty + error-propagation cases, and exact SQL/params assertions via toHaveBeenCalledWith.

The leave_policies table schema (id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at; no foreign keys) and the dependency map (policy → shared/types, policy → shared/db only) must match the reconciled architecture exactly.

integrationPoints.why: LeavePolicy.leaveType is typed as the LeaveType enum imported from shared/types — the policy module's only shared-types dependency.
PolicyRepository uses the existing pg Pool export for all database access — the policy module's only shared-db dependency.

The balance module will depend on the policy module's public barrel to look up LeavePolicy entitlement and accrual configuration; the barrel must expose LeavePolicy and the repository interface for downstream constructor injection.
The leave orchestrator will resolve LeavePolicy by leaveTypeId to enforce minimumNoticeDays and requiresManagerApproval rules; it consumes the policy module only through its index.ts barrel.
